body:
## Summary

Clang's `-Rpass-missed=inline` showed that `json_value::destroy`, the copy constructor and scalar comparisons are never inlined (about 380 call sites), even for scalars. This PR keeps the scalar path inline and moves the owning/general paths into never-inlined helpers:

- `destroy(value_t)`: inline "owns memory?" test, work in `destroy_owned()`
- copy constructor: inline union copy for null/bool/numbers/discarded, `copy_owning()` otherwise (nesting guard unchanged)
- `==`, `<` (C++11–17) and `==`, `<=>` (C++20): inline same-type scalar fast path (`JSON_IMPLEMENT_SCALAR_FAST`); the old bodies move to `equal_general`, `less_general`, `three_way_general`. The same-type scalar cases are shared with `JSON_IMPLEMENT_OPERATOR` via `JSON_IMPLEMENT_SCALAR_CASES`, with every `value_t` enumerator still listed (`-Wswitch-enum`). Mixed types, NaN, discarded and `JSON_USE_LEGACY_DISCARDED_VALUE_COMPARISON` still take the general path
- `json_value(value_t)`: allocating cases in `init_owned()`

Coordination: only the `destroy()` dispatch is touched, so it merges cleanly with #5835 (`destroy_container`).

## Numbers (ns/op unless noted, best of 9, -O2, Apple clang 21 / GCC 16.2)

| benchmark | clang before | clang after | GCC before | GCC after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `json j = 42` | 1.31 | 0.48 | 0.66 | 0.58 |
| scalar copy | 2.90 | 1.01 | 2.16 | 0.90 |
| `j == 5` | 3.55 | 0.65 | 2.27 | 0.64 |
| `j < 3.0` | 3.54 | 0.65 | 2.59 | 0.64 |
| `vector<json>` 1M ints build+destroy (ms) | 3.53 | 1.06 | 1.36 | 1.16 |
| canada copy+destroy (ms) | 3.19 | 2.90 | 3.53 | 3.29 |
| canada `==` (µs) | 540 | 459 | 601 | 639 |
| citm `==` (µs) | 300 | 301 | 363 | 388 |
| canada parse (ms) | 9.23 | 8.94 | 9.26 | 8.85 |

Caveats: with GCC, `==` on large documents is ~7 % slower. A scalar move-then-reassign loop shows +8 % on GCC (1.63 → 1.75 ns); GCC emits the same `strb`+`str` → `ldp` sequence in the base, so this is a pre-existing store-forwarding pattern that is merely more visible once the rest of the loop gets cheaper. Code size on a probe TU grows by 13 % at -O2 and 6 % at -Os.

## Testing

New tests: `unit-comparison.cpp` ("comparison of scalars (inline fast path)": same/mixed number types incl. negative vs. unsigned, bool/null, string vs. number, NaN incl. `<=>`, discarded, scalar overloads) and `unit-constructor2.cpp` (copy of scalar vs. string/array/object/binary then mutate, `vector<json>` of mixed types).


Full ctest (146 tests, ASan+UBSan, clang) passes. Additionally unit-comparison with `-std=c++11/20` and with `JSON_USE_LEGACY_DISCARDED_VALUE_COMPARISON`, unit-diagnostics and regression2 with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1`. No new `-Weverything` warnings. `make amalgamate` run.

## Breaking changes

None. No public API, ABI tag or behaviour changes; the new helpers are private.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann. Changes since the approval (047c7ea01):

- **Shared macro:** the same-type scalar cases now live in one sub-macro, `JSON_IMPLEMENT_SCALAR_CASES`, used by both `JSON_IMPLEMENT_OPERATOR` and `JSON_IMPLEMENT_SCALAR_FAST`. All enumerators stay listed. Clean with the CI flag sets (`-Weverything` for clang, the full `gcc_flags.cmake` list for GCC 16) in C++11/17/20. Timings are unchanged: best of 15, alternating builds, Apple clang and GCC 16, -O2. `j==5` ≈ 183 ms vs 185 ms (clang) and 180 vs 193 ms (GCC); `==`/`<` on scalars and `==` on canada.json are within noise on both.
- **Placement:** `copy_owning`, `equal_general`, `less_general` and `three_way_general` moved into the existing private sections, so no `private:`/`public:` toggles remain in the middle of the public API. No public declaration moved.
- **Tests:** scalar comparison (number types incl. negative vs. unsigned, bool/null, string vs. number, NaN incl. `<=>`, discarded, scalar overloads) and copy/destroy of every value type (including a `vector<json>` of mixed types).

Ran unit-comparison (C++11/20), unit-constructor1/2, unit-diagnostics with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1` and unit-allocator locally; all pass. Description updated; no breaking changes.

review_comments.body: Good catch, and yes: GCC's `-Wswitch-enum` (enabled in `cmake/gcc_flags.cmake`) warns about unlisted enumerators even with a `default:` label. I had dropped the explicit cases to silence clang's `-Wcovered-switch-default`, which is already disabled in `cmake/clang_flags.cmake`. The enumerators are listed again in 1 new commit; with that, `-Wswitch`/`-Wswitch-enum`/`-Wswitch-default` give no warnings for GCC 16 or clang. (Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)

review_comments.body:
Fixed in 5db395b33: `destroy()` and the copy constructor now call a new `detail::owns_memory(value_t)` in `value_t.hpp`. It is a `switch` that lists every enumerator, so `-Wswitch-enum` flags it when a type is added, and the owning set is defined in one place.

Performance: with Clang (-O2) both forms compile to the same code, a single bitmask test (`1 << t & 0x10E`). With GCC 16 the `switch` version costs one or two extra branches on the scalar path, which is negligible next to the gain from inlining the check.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Fixed in 5db395b33: the copy constructor now uses `!detail::owns_memory(m_data.m_type)` (see the reply above).

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

`copy_owning()` is only reached for types where `owns_memory()` is true, so its `if` only splits the owning types into containers (copied iteratively by `copy_structured()`) and strings/binaries (`copy_leaf_value()`). A new type would first have to be added to `owns_memory()` to get here, which `-Wswitch-enum` now enforces. So I left this one as it is.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

No, removed in 5db395b33. They are only needed for the container operands, where GCC otherwise parses `array <` as `std::array<` (#1530/#590). The comment above `JSON_IMPLEMENT_OPERATOR` now says that. I kept `(null_result)` because it is a macro parameter.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Yes, astyle pads the brackets when a line ends in `<`. In 5db395b33 the container types get their own aliases and the trait is `detail::conjunction<std::is_same<...>, std::is_same<...>>` on one line, which astyle leaves alone.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

Yes, intentional, but the shared name was misleading. Renamed to `equal_leaf()` in 5db395b33, with a note explaining the difference: inside the container walk, strings are the most common leaves, so comparing them inline pays off. In the top-level operators, `JSON_IMPLEMENT_SCALAR_FAST` leaves them out to keep the code inlined at each call site small. Binary values are rare and go to `equal_general()` in both.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

title: Make the value lifecycle inline-friendly
